findings.title: Privacy branches never pass the connected wallet to WalletAttempts
findings.description: The privacy implementation filters the journal by an optional wallet prop and hides all account/hash/clear controls when it is absent. Every production caller still renders WalletAttempts without that prop. Connecting a wallet therefore cannot reveal those journal rows or their explicit-clear action.
findings.impact: Journal history and recovery controls are unavailable in the affected branches. The duplicate-attempt journal still blocks retries, so unresolved attempts can leave users stuck without the intended recovery action. A transaction hash may still be visible in the current transaction view. No theft, false success or loss of journal protection is established.
findings.recommendation: Pass the live connected account and chain from every caller, remove the scope immediately on disconnect/account/chain changes, and preserve the separate PrivateHistory reveal and explicit-clear consent.
acceptance_criteria: Route-level tests for Pay and Registry must exercise the actual caller wiring: disconnected journal stays masked; connecting the matching account/chain makes only its rows eligible for a deliberate reveal; changing identity hides them again.
An unknown attempt must continue blocking a duplicate request until the explicit clear action is confirmed; privacy controls must not silently clear journal state.

evidence.supports: Optional wallet prop controls visibility and clear controls.
Invoice-load caller omits wallet.
Payment caller omits wallet.
Registry caller omits wallet.
Experimental policy caller also omits wallet.
Component tests supply wallet manually and therefore do not cover the missing route integration.

findings.title: Bill print stylesheet hides receipt print content
findings.category: Product correctness; no security impact established
findings.status: Confirmed CSS cascade and import-chain conflict; browser print not executed
findings.branch_scope: All 20 selected heads; identical print.css, app.css and PrintableBill.tsx blobs
findings.description: AppShell eagerly imports Pay; Pay imports PrintBillButton; PrintableBill statically imports print.css. Its print-media body descendant rule hides every element with !important and restores visibility only for bill-sheet. The receipt-print visibility rule in app.css lacks !important. ReceiptPanel calls window.print directly for receipt-print content, so that content remains hidden under the globally loaded bill stylesheet, regardless of stylesheet ordering.
findings.impact: Receipt print output has no visible receipt content (blank output is the expected browser result). On-screen receipt data, JSON export and signatures are unaffected by this cascade finding. No browser or printer reproduction was performed.
findings.recommendation: Use an explicit active print target or a shared print stylesheet that scopes visibility rules to the selected bill or receipt. Ensure only the chosen print target is restored.
acceptance_criteria: Validate the computed print-media visibility and generated output of both bill and receipt actions in the same application bundle.
The selected bill/receipt must print; unrelated page content, raw JSON and action controls must remain excluded.

evidence.supports: Eager import of Pay.
Static import of PrintBillButton.
Global static import of print.css.
Important global hidden rule and bill-only visibility exception.
Receipt visibility exception is non-important.
Receipt uses receipt-print and a direct window.print action.
Existing test body checks bill output/style text and print invocation, not the combined receipt CSS cascade.

findings.title: Merchant export duplicate invoice detection depends on sort adjacency
findings.category: Accounting data integrity in ancillary package
findings.status: Confirmed source-level defect; no web consumer found
findings.description: resolveAll sorts invoices primarily by createdAt and only compares adjacent ids. Duplicate ids at different timestamps can be separated by another invoice after sorting and escape the advertised duplicate-invoice rejection. All export formats and the tax summary consume resolveAll.
findings.impact: Callers can receive repeated invoice identifiers and duplicated totals in exports or summaries. Current repository consumers are in the paused CLI; no apps/web import was found. This is not an established current web payment vulnerability.
findings.recommendation: Check invoice-id uniqueness with a set or map independently of the output sort, then keep the deterministic date/id ordering.
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate identifiers must be rejected independent of input order, differing creation dates and intervening records.
Every exporter and taxSummary must enforce the same uniqueness invariant.

evidence.supports: Date-first ordering with adjacent-only duplicate check.
CSV uses the affected resolver.
Tax totals use the same affected resolver.
Existing duplicate test covers adjacent equal-date duplicates.
Only discovered production importer belongs to the paused CLI.

findings.title: Experimental PolicyPay input edits do not invalidate an in-flight review guard
findings.branch_scope: Both PolicyPay variants across selected heads; experimental policy off by default and no pinned deployment
findings.description: PolicyPay captures a prepared transaction and a guard bound to session and deployment. After send begins and awaits RPC/other work, the meta-address, token and amount fields remain editable. Their handlers clear rendered reviewed state but do not invalidate the captured guard or prepared object used by the existing send closure. Reviewing again also does not advance a guard revision. The send library checks captured transaction bytes against its captured review, not against the new visible inputs.
findings.impact: If the policy feature is activated with a deployment, an operation already in progress can continue with an older review after the user edits the displayed terms. Wallet confirmation still exists; this is not a proven bypass of wallet approval. No active production exposure is claimed because PINNED_POLICY_DEPLOYMENTS is empty.
findings.recommendation: Before activation, bind each review/send operation to a live UI revision and invalidate it on input change, replacement review and unmount; alternatively prevent edits throughout the pre-handoff operation. Check the revision immediately before wallet handoff and preserve truthful post-handoff outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: An edit to recipient/meta-address, token or amount while awaiting authorization/RPC/allowance work must prevent any subsequent wallet request for the superseded review.
A newer review must not revive an older in-flight operation, and a response from a request already handed to the wallet must still be journaled truthfully.

evidence.supports: Review guard captures only session/deployment and send retains captured review across awaits.
Payment inputs and Review remain enabled during busy; input handlers only clear React state.
Downstream checks use the captured guard and review.
Empty production deployment allowlist limits current reachability.
Experimental feature remains off by default.

retired_hypotheses.title: TagVault plaintext returned after a session switch
retired_hypotheses.reason: Mounted production AppShell synchronously calls services.vault.lock on subscribeSession events, invalidating the revision before in-flight tag operations can release results. TagArchive also guards its async operations. Custody reviewer confirmed the integration.

retired_hypotheses.title: PolicyView record reuse across ordinary seller replacement
retired_hypotheses.reason: The ordinary seller replacement flow requires navigating away to SellerKeys, which unmounts PolicyView and drops its local records. No reachable production path for the same-mounted-component hypothesis was demonstrated.

retired_hypotheses.title: Policy action clearing uses key instead of id
retired_hypotheses.reason: duplicateAttemptJournal.clearAttempt explicitly accepts either an attempt id or an attempt key.

historical_notes: Main transport defaults and non-finite retry option handling differ from integration; integration rpc.ts adds credential/referrer/cache restrictions and a finite retry guard. These are existing hardening deltas, not a newly established production exploit.
Main jitter uses a wall-clock-only expiry check; latest adds a monotonic floor. No external clock-rollback path was established.

Main merchant reconciliation could mark a zero-payment invoice paid when tolerance covered the amount; integration fixes the positive-payment invariant. Avoid duplicate reporting against earlier D-2 notes.

Prior wave payment_ui_review.json contains distinct receipt hash/status, ERC20 simulation, sweep review authority, QR lifecycle and runtime helper findings; keep their branch-specific status rather than collapsing them into this wave.
